answer: An agent economy can run a lagoon of minting rights: each identity pays a stake priced on a convex curve tied to its funder, so the k-th clone from one wallet costs k² times the first — a thousand identities cost a million-fold more than one. Funds lock for a tenure as slow to weather as basalt, so a single pool of capital cannot mint clones in series. And when one identity misbehaves, slashing burns its whole minted family at once, the way a juniper stand dies together because all stems share one root system.
